correctness.rationale: Pointwise least-period Möbius inversion gives the exact integer character sum over period subgroups. A character not annihilating the shortest squarefree-kernel-period subgroup vanishes termwise; every annihilating character receives its nonzero shortest-period term and the largest surviving integer power of q strictly dominates all smaller powers. The explicit two-coordinate inverse-character witness attains q^b. Every multiplier is a multiple of q^b, and the trivial multiplier is the positive primitive-word count. Fourier diagonalization, complete annihilator support and duality prove ranks, stabilizer, range and projection. Exact binary/ternary/cyclic-four/Klein-four enumerations passed; finite tests only corroborate the universal proof.

Closest primitive-word degree-one sampling has a different operator and cannot by itself imply all higher-frequency nonvanishing.

value.rationale: Aperiodic rooted words are canonical coding/orbit objects, and the full convolution kernel and sharp stability determine which configuration signals can be recovered. The squarefree kernel n/rad(n) gives a qualitatively different information-loss rate at squarefree versus prime-power lengths. Exact stabilizer, rank q^(n-b), minimum q^b and explicit recovered quotient are natural structural invariants for all lengths and all finite abelian alphabets; they are not merely the classical primitive-word count or a narrow finite numerical slice.
